title: Autonote constructor and ephemeral trace extractor for compact oncall artifacts
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds an automatic incident note constructor and a compact, redacted ephemeral trace extractor used by the incident-bot to surface concise diagnostics to oncall. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Oncall responders frequently ask for a compact, privacy-safe snapshot (short note + trace snippet) in the first 2 minutes of an incident. This PR adds two cooperating pieces: (1) an "Autonote Constructor" that builds a short human-readable incident summary from alert metadata, top traces, and the highest-scoring evidence; and (2) an Ephemeral Trace Extractor that pulls a bounded stack/event window from traces, applies redaction rules, and returns a compact, formatted digest that can be attached to a note or used in a Slack pager message.

What changed (high level): implemented a new pkg/autonote package with a rule-based summarizer, added a trace extractor service that runs locally in the bot process under a strict CPU/time budget, integrated both into the incident-bot pipeline (signals -> evidence -> autonote). The autonote output includes: title (one line), 2-3 bullet keypoints ranked by confidence, and a short list of implicated services. The trace extractor returns up to 3 trace spans with contextual logs (redacted). Both components include configuration knobs (max_tokens, redaction_policy, sampling_rate) exposed in the bot config and defaults tuned for low overhead.

Checklist:
- [x] prototype summarizer with deterministic heuristics
- [x] redaction-first extractor + unit tests
- [x] end-to-end e2e using incident-sim with synthetic traces
- [x] privacy review and PII redaction rules added to policy config
- [x] documentation: incident-bot/README and runbook samples
- [x] metrics and tracing for autonote latency and extractor CPU/memory

Testing: unit tests for rule coverage, property tests for redaction (PII patterns), integration tests that simulate noisy traces and validate that output size is bounded and contains no email/SSN patterns. Local load runs confirmed average autonote construction time 120ms (p95 360ms) on staging bot instance with existing mem/cpu budget.

Rollback plan: flag-gated under runtime config `enable_autonote_v1`. If issues are observed, toggle the flag to disable autonomic note construction; the bot will continue to create the previous minimal attachments.

Notes on privacy/security: extractor applies a two-stage redaction: pattern-based removal for common PII and a whitelist of safe keys from trace annotations. Redaction is applied before any content is serialized to logs or sent to external channels. Audit logs added for every extraction event (trace_id, redaction_summary, size_bytes) to help compliance review.

Related: ENG-4591 defines the acceptance criteria for early incident artifacts, SRE-124 requested the compact trace snippets in Slack-based pagers. SUP-887 was the support ticket that motivated an immediate safety-first deploy for a recent pager noise incident.

Lena Zhou (reviewer): Two suggestions: (1) make the default max_tokens 256 to reduce tokenization overhead; (2) add opt-out for teams that already have pager attachments.
